The average treatment effect on the control (ATC) is about 3.60. I estimated it by fitting a linear regression of the outcome on all 25 covariates among the treated children only. I then used that model to predict what each control child's score would have been with treatment. The ATC is the average of those predicted scores minus the observed control scores.

I picked this method because the data come from an observational study, so the raw difference in means may be confounded. For comparison, the raw difference in means is 3.66. A single regression on the full sample with a treatment indicator gives 3.95.

ANSWER: 3.60
